subject: Clarify spend caps and overage policy for Lumen Analytics
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@lumenanalytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Lumen Analytics Procurement <procurement@lumenanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Baseline pricing + what happens if we spike past budget

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile. I have two quick asks as we prepare an internal recommendation: 1) can you send the current hosted API rate card (per-token generation + embeddings baseline) that you'd recommend for our expected volume, and 2) what is Redwood's operational approach if we exceed a monthly budget cap?

Specifically: does Redwood automatically block traffic, throttle, charge overage at list rate, or provide a grace period? Our security & procurement teams are sensitive to unexpected bills and want options that prevent surprise charges.

We plan to present a conservative forecast to procurement; if you can include the standard mechanisms you offer (hard caps, alerts, prepay credits, invoice billing thresholds) and any recommended guardrails, that would be super helpful.

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
Product Manager, Lumen Analytics
Attachment: none
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@lumenanalytics.com>
Cc: Lumen Analytics Procurement <procurement@lumenanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Nov 2025 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Baseline pricing + what happens if we spike past budget

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our current hosted rate card and a short note on operational guardrails. High level: we support both preventive and reactive controls.

Quick bullets so you can paste into the procurement deck:
- Rate card (attached): per-token gen / embeddings baseline, plus volume tiers.
- Hard spend cap: we can configure an account-level hard cap to block additional requests when a monthly spend threshold is reached (no charges beyond that month).
- Soft cap + throttling: account can be configured to continue accepting requests up to a soft buffer, with automatic token-rate throttling and detailed event notifications.
- Prepay / committed usage: credits are consumed first; if credits run out, behavior follows whichever cap policy is active (hard block or soft throttling + invoice).
- Auto-billing (default): if enabled, any overage beyond prepaid credits is billed on the next invoice at the agreed rate. We typically require PO + net30 for invoice billing.
- Alerts & hooks: webhooks and paged alerts available for spend thresholds (configurable at 50%, 75%, 90%).

If you want, we can propose two guardrail bundles: (A) "Procurement-safe" with hard cap + prepay credits + webhook alerts; (B) "Business-continuity" with soft cap + throttling + invoice overage (with negotiated overage discount).

Sending the rate card now. CC'ing our finance lead Marcus to confirm discounting and billing flex.

Attachment: Redwood-Rate-Card-202511.pdf (application/pdf, 92KB)

—
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Baseline pricing + what happens if we spike past budget (internal)

Rachel / Vanessa — quick internal note. For Lumen (mid-market, predictable growth), I'm comfortable offering:
- 10% first-year committed usage discount if they sign a 12-mo committed plan (prepay or monthly invoiced with PO).
- Soft cap default, with the option to enable hard cap at procurement request. If they want auto-billing + overage invoice, finance needs the PO and billing contact on file.

A couple of caveats:
- Hard caps are operationally safe but may cause API errors for the app if they spike; CS must pre-agree fallback (e.g., degraded prompt, cached responses).
- If we grant a discount, we should limit the auto-overage discount (no more than 5% on overage) to avoid open-ended exposure.

Rachel — if you want me to formalize language I can draft a short redline for the SOW.

Marcus
Director, Finance Operations
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@lumenanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Baseline pricing + what happens if we spike past budget

Hi all — looping back from CS/ops perspective. Two operational recommendations if Lumen wants minimal risk of application disruption:
1) Enable webhook spend alerts at 50/75/90% + a 24-hour automatic throttle window that reduces token throughput by ~60% when the 100% soft threshold is hit. This avoids a hard outage but slows throughput predictably.
2) If they choose a hard cap, we will return 429-style errors once the cap is hit; recommend pairing with client-side retry/backoff and a cached fallback prompt.

We can also configure a temporary "emergency buffer" (one-time, Finance-approved credit) that CS can apply to resume service while procurement finalizes additional budget. Marcus — can we pre-authorize up to $5k emergency buffer for this account?

—Vanessa
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@lumenanalytics.com>, Lumen Analytics Procurement <procurement@lumenanalytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Baseline pricing + what happens if we spike past budget — proposed options

Sara / procurement team — thank you for the question and for your patience while we pulled internal alignment. Below is a short summary you can include in your procurement deck. I also attached the rate card referenced earlier.

Option 1 — Procurement-safe (recommended for strict budget controls)
- Prepay credits or committed monthly spend.
- Hard spend cap enabled at your requested threshold.
- Webhook + email alerts at 50/75/90%.
- Result: once cap is hit, additional API requests are blocked (no overage charges).

Option 2 — Business-continuity (recommended if uninterrupted service is critical)
- Prepay credits OR invoice billing with PO + net30.
- Soft cap + throttling: service continues with reduced token throughput once the soft threshold is reached.
- Auto-billing for any overage at agreed rate; we can offer a 5% overage discount if a 12-mo commitment is signed.

Operational notes
- Emergency buffer: we can provide a one-time, finance-approved buffer (up to $5,000) to avoid immediate outage while procurement processes additional funds.
- If hard cap is enabled, the client app must handle 429s gracefully; CS will work with your engineers on best-effort fallback behaviors.

Next steps
1) Tell us which option (1 or 2) you prefer and the threshold amount for the cap.
2) If you want the 10% first-year committed discount, Marcus will prepare the SOW language and discount conditions.
3) Procurement: if invoice billing is required, please share the PO contact + billing address so finance can set net30 terms.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through tradeoffs.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood-Rate-Card-202511.pdf (application/pdf, 92KB)
